newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HKMA urges cooperation among Asian central banks.
newsitem.headline: HKMA urges cooperation among Asian central banks.

text.p: A top official of Hong Kong's de facto central bank said on Monday divergent Asian economies put in a strong case for monetary segregation but argued that there could still be scope for cooperation in the region.

"Divergence rather than convergence argues for monetary segregation in this region," Joseph Yam, chief executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, told a conference gathering of bankers in the region sponsored by I.D.E.A.
"But we still need...a range of monetary controls to deliver stability, we still need intensive mechanisms for minimising as much as possible the risks and managing those risks," he said.
"I think the solution at the regional level is the creation of what I would like to call the Asian monetary network."

Yam argued that while social, political, economic and monetary diversities between regional economies made a union such as the European Monetary Union less feasible in Asia, countries in the region could still cooperate.
"But there are quite a number of issues concerning the financial infrastructure of this region where a network and closer cooperation can be (effected)."
One example, he said, was the creation of bilateral pacts among Asian central banks to repurchase U.S. treasuries.
The agreements followed closely the Mexican financial crisis in 1995, when central banks in the region saw the need to boost liquidity when they need to stabilise their currencies.
Yam said while there was still no clear concensus on a number of issues, there was growing momentum among Asian economies to cooperate closely.
"There is in fact a very interesting plan...for these bilateral repos to be multilaterlised in some sort of facility," he said, but did not provide details how that might be done.

Other possible areas of cooperation were the linking up of an on-line payment system now being individually developed in Asian countries, and the linkage of their debt clearing systems which would help bolster investments in the region and minimise risks, Yam said.
